title: Spring Boot E-Commerce API – Auth & JWT Flow
context: This session covers the registration flow, password encoding, JWT generation, and Spring Security configuration of the E-Commerce API project. All questions are answered by reading the provided code snippets and reasoning about control flow.

acceptance_criteria: States the password is NOT stored in plain text; BCrypt encoding is applied via encoder.encode()
States the JWT subject is the user's email address

rubric.criterion: Password encoding explanation (BCrypt, not plain text)

questions.solution_notes: Role defaults to User.Role.USER in the builder. The encoder bean is a BCryptPasswordEncoder from SecurityConfig, so the stored password is BCrypt-hashed. JwtUtil.generateToken() calls .setSubject(email), making email the JWT subject.

acceptance_criteria: States the token expires 1 hour (3600000 ms = 1 hour) after generation
States isTokenValid() returns false when token is expired because parseClaimsJws() throws an ExpiredJwtException which is caught
Identifies at least one risk of catching broad Exception (e.g., swallowing unexpected errors silently, treating all exceptions as invalid tokens)

rubric.criterion: isTokenValid return value on expired token with explanation

questions.solution_notes: 3600000 ms = 60 min = 1 hour. parseClaimsJws throws ExpiredJwtException (a JwtException subclass) on expiry; the catch returns false. Catching Exception hides programming bugs, e.g. NullPointerException would silently return false instead of surfacing the real error.

questions.prompt:
Study the SecurityConfig below.

```java
http
    .csrf(csrf -> csrf.disable())
    .authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth
        .requestMatchers("/api/auth/**").permitAll()
        .requestMatchers("/api/auth/**", "/error","/registernew").permitAll()
        .anyRequest().authenticated());
```

(a) The route `/api/auth/**` appears in TWO separate `.requestMatchers()` calls. Is this a bug or harmless duplication? Explain the effect.
(b) Is `/api/products` accessible without authentication? Why or why not?
(c) CSRF protection is disabled. In what scenario is this acceptable, and when would it be a security risk?
acceptance_criteria: Identifies the duplicate matcher as harmless redundancy (second rule is never reached for /api/auth/** since it already matches first); no security hole introduced
States /api/products is NOT accessible without authentication (it falls through to anyRequest().authenticated())
States CSRF disable is acceptable for stateless REST APIs using JWT tokens; would be a risk for browser-based session-cookie apps

rubric.criterion: CSRF trade-off explanation (stateless JWT vs session cookies)

questions.solution_notes: Spring Security processes rules in order; the first matching rule wins. /api/auth/** is already permitted by the first matcher, so the second rule for it is dead code but harmless. /api/products matches anyRequest().authenticated(). CSRF tokens are not needed when the API is stateless and uses Authorization header tokens because CSRF exploits rely on browsers automatically sending session cookies.

questions.prompt:
The project has stub classes for CartService, OrderService, and ProductController (empty bodies). You notice AuthController only has a /register endpoint, but there is no /login endpoint.

(a) What happens if a registered user tries to call a protected route like `/api/products`? Trace the flow using SecurityConfig, JwtUtil, and the current AuthController.
(b) What is the minimum code you would need to add to support JWT-authenticated login (not implementation – just describe which class to modify and what it needs to do)?
acceptance_criteria: States the user will receive a 401/403 or a block because there is no JWT filter wired into the security chain
Describes adding a /login endpoint to AuthController that verifies credentials and returns a token via JwtUtil.generateToken()
Mentions adding a JWT filter (OncePerRequestFilter) to SecurityConfig to extract and validate the token on each request

rubric.criterion: Correctly traces the missing filter gap (401/403 response)
Identifies need for JWT request filter in SecurityConfig

questions.solution_notes: Even if a token was registered, SecurityConfig has no JWT filter (e.g. UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter replacement or OncePerRequestFilter). Without extracting and setting the SecurityContext, every /api/products call fails with 403. The fix requires: (1) a POST /api/auth/login in AuthController that accepts email+password, verifies via PasswordEncoder.matches(), and returns a JWT; (2) a JwtAuthFilter extending OncePerRequestFilter that reads the Authorization header, validates the token, and sets the authentication in SecurityContextHolder; (3) registering that filter before UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter in SecurityConfig.
